--- title: "[StreamingGAM]{.doc-object-name .doc-class .doc-label .doc-label-class}" body-classes: doc-api-page page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Streaming / online GAM. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/whittaker/blob/main/whittaker/streaming.py#L70-L665){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.CLASS} ```python StreamingGAM(formula, *, family=None, decay=1.0, smoothing_params=None) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} Fits a GAM incrementally by accumulating weighted sufficient statistics (`X'WX` and `X'Wz`) across data batches, rather than storing and re-fitting on the full dataset each time. This makes it suitable for data arriving continuously or in a stream too large to hold in memory at once: the memory footprint depends only on the number of basis coefficients `p` (via a `p x p` matrix), not on the number of observations seen. The model structure (formula, basis dimensions, penalties) is fixed at initialisation from a small pilot batch, and subsequent `partial_fit()` calls add data without storing the raw observations. Two update modes are supported: **accumulate mode** (`decay=1.0`, the default), where every batch contributes equally regardless of when it arrived, and **sliding-window mode** (`decay < 1.0`), where older batches' contributions to the accumulated statistics are exponentially downweighted, allowing the model to adapt to a slowly drifting data-generating process. Use `StreamingGAM` for large or continuously-arriving datasets where holding the full data in memory (as ordinary `GAM` does) is impractical, or where the underlying relationship may drift over time and old data should be forgotten. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [formula]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str | Formula]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Model formula (e.g. `"y ~ s(x1) + s(x2)"`). [family]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Family | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Response distribution family. Defaults to `Gaussian()`. [decay]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[1.0]{.fl}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Exponential decay factor for sliding window. `1.0` (default) means no decay (accumulate all data equally). Values less than `1.0` downweight older batches' sufficient statistics by a factor of `decay` every time a new batch arrives. [smoothing_params]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [list[float] | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Fixed smoothing parameters. If `None`, estimated from the pilot batch (via a one-off ordinary `GAM` fit with REML) and optionally re-estimated later via `solve(reestimate_smoothing=True)`. ::: ## Notes {.doc-notes} Each `partial_fit()` call treats the incoming batch as one step of iteratively reweighted least squares: given the current coefficients, it computes working responses `z` and IRLS weights `W` for the batch, forms the batch's contribution to the weighted normal equations, $$X_{\text{batch}}' W X_{\text{batch}}, \qquad X_{\text{batch}}' W z_{\text{batch}},$$ and adds these to the running totals (after applying the decay factor, if any, to the existing totals). Calling `solve()` then solves the penalized normal equations $$\left(\sum_{\text{batches}} X'WX + S_\lambda\right) \beta = \sum_{\text{batches}} X'Wz$$ via a Cholesky factorization, where `S_\lambda = \sum_j \lambda_j S_j` is the weighted sum of penalty matrices. Because only the accumulated `p x p` matrix `X'WX` and length-`p` vector `X'Wz` are retained, this scales to arbitrarily many observations at fixed memory cost in `p`. ## Examples {.doc-examples} ::: {#8933fd4a .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import numpy as np from whittaker.streaming import StreamingGAM rng = np.random.default_rng(0) model = StreamingGAM("y ~ s(x)") for _ in range(5): x = rng.uniform(0, 1, 200) y = np.sin(2 * np.pi * x) + rng.normal(scale=0.2, size=200) model.partial_fit({"x": x, "y": y}) model.solve() print(model.summary()) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` StreamingGAM summary ============================================================ Formula: y ~ s(x) Family: Gaussian Decay: 1.0 N obs: 1000 N batches: 5 EDF total: 9.6 Scale: 0.3044 Deviance: 301.5 Smooth terms: s(x): edf=8.6 Snapshots: 1 ``` ::: ::: ## Attributes {.doc-attributes}
Name Description
coefficients Current coefficient vector from the most recent `solve()` (or the pilot fit).
edf_total Total effective degrees of freedom from the most recent `solve()`.
family Response distribution family used for the link function and variance model.
formula Parsed model formula this streaming GAM was constructed with.
is_initialised Whether the model structure has been built from a pilot batch.
is_solved Whether coefficients are available from an initial fit or a `solve()` call.
n_batches Total number of batches passed to `partial_fit()` so far.
n_obs Accumulated observation count across all ingested batches.
scale Estimated dispersion (scale) parameter from the most recent `solve()`.
smoothing_params Smoothing parameters currently in use, one per penalized smooth term.

Returns a copy, so mutating the returned list does not affect the model. ::: ## Methods {.doc-methods}
Name Description
partial_fit() Ingest a batch of data.

should_refit() Check if a refit (solve) is recommended.

### [partial_fit()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} ::: {.doc-subject} Ingest a batch of data. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/whittaker/blob/main/whittaker/streaming.py#L316-L380){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python partial_fit(data) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} On the first call, builds the model matrix structure (basis dimensions, penalties, knot locations) from this batch via a pilot `GAM` fit, and initializes the coefficients and smoothing parameters from that fit (unless fixed smoothing parameters were supplied). Subsequent calls reuse this fixed structure: the batch's working response and IRLS weights are computed using the *current* coefficients (from the most recent `solve()`, or the pilot fit), and its contribution to the running `X'WX` / `X'Wz` sufficient statistics is added (after applying the decay factor to existing totals, if `decay < 1.0`). ::: #### Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [data]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [InputData]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Column-oriented batch data containing the response and all covariates in `formula`. ::: #### Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [StreamingGAM]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Returns `self` for method chaining. ::: ### [predict()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} ::: {.doc-subject} Predict on new data. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/whittaker/blob/main/whittaker/streaming.py#L525-L568){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python predict(new_data, *, se=False) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} Builds the prediction design matrix using the fixed basis structure established at initialisation, and forms the linear predictor and (via the family's inverse link) fitted values from the current coefficients. Requires that `solve()` has been called at least once. ::: #### Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [new_data]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [InputData]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Column-oriented covariate data. [se]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[False]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True`, compute standard errors on the linear predictor scale from the Bayesian posterior covariance implied by the current accumulated `X'WX` and smoothing parameters. ::: #### Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [PredictionResult]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : ::: ### [reset()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} ::: {.doc-subject} Reset accumulated statistics (keep model structure). ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/whittaker/blob/main/whittaker/streaming.py#L629-L648){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python reset() ``` ::: #### Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [StreamingGAM]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : ::: ### min_batches=10) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} Returns `True` when enough new data has accumulated since the last solve to justify re-estimating coefficients. ::: #### Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [min_batches]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[10]{.dv}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Minimum batches since last solve before recommending refit. ::: ### [smoothing_history()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} ::: {.doc-subject} Return history of snapshots taken at each `solve()` call. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/whittaker/blob/main/whittaker/streaming.py#L586-L593){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python smoothing_history() ``` ::: #### Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [list[StreamingSnapshot]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : ::: ### [solve()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} ::: {.doc-subject} Solve for coefficients from accumulated sufficient statistics. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/whittaker/blob/main/whittaker/streaming.py#L406-L473){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python solve(*, reestimate_smoothing=False) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} Forms the penalized normal equations `(X'WX + S_lambda) beta = X'Wz` from the currently accumulated statistics and the current smoothing parameters, and solves them via a Cholesky factorization (with a small ridge added for numerical stability). Also updates effective degrees of freedom, the scale estimate, and appends a `StreamingSnapshot` to the fit history. ::: #### Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [reestimate_smoothing]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[False]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True`, re-estimate smoothing parameters from the current sufficient statistics using a GCV line search over each smoothing parameter in turn (coordinate-wise). Default `False` uses the current (pilot or fixed) smoothing parameters. Ignored (has no effect) if the model was constructed with fixed `smoothing_params`. ::: #### Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [StreamingGAM]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Returns `self` for method chaining. ::: ### [summary()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} ::: {.doc-subject} Build a human-readable text summary of the streaming GAM's current state. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/whittaker/blob/main/whittaker/streaming.py#L595-L627){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python summary() ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} Reports the formula, family, decay factor, accumulated observation and batch counts, total EDF, scale, and accumulated deviance, followed by a per-smooth-term EDF breakdown and the number of `solve()` snapshots recorded so far. ::: #### Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Multi-line summary text. :::
